title: Cech vanishing from surjectivity onto unions of cover intersections
statement: Let $Y$ be a topological space, $F$ an abelian sheaf on its open site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $\mathcal U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open covering $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ of an open subset $U\subseteq Y$, indexed by a set $I$. For each finite nonempty $J\subseteq I$ put $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j$. Assume that for every family $\mathcal S$ of finite nonempty subsets of $I$, the restriction map $F(U)\longrightarrow F(\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal S}U_J)$ is surjective, including $\mathcal S=\varnothing$. Then $\check H^p(\mathcal U,F)=0$ for every $p>0$. Here Cech cohomology is that of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] on the open site: degree $p\geq0$ is $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}F(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p})$, with the alternating sum of restriction maps as differential, including tuples with repetitions. No finiteness of $I$, compactness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi (statement, lines 1999-2007); intersections indexed by tuples are the same as finite nonempty subsets after removing repetitions.

proof.text: Use the space P of finite nonempty subsets of I, with its upper-set topology for inclusion, enlarged by ULift to Type (max v w). For finite J let B_J be the open of finite nonempty sets containing J. In particular B_{singleton i} are opens and intersections indexed by a nonempty finite tuple are B_J for the set J of its entries. Every point A has the principal open B_A as smallest neighborhood. This finite-point variant of the source construction suffices: all principal opens used there already have finite nonempty index.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi, proof; finite-nonempty-subset variant of the auxiliary space

proof.text: Define T(Z) as the union of U_J over all finite nonempty J whose point belongs to Z. This equals the union of U_J over B_J contained in Z because Z is upper. It is monotone, T(Z) is contained in U, and T(B_J)=U_J for nonempty J. The union J union K shows T(Z intersection W)=T(Z) intersection T(W). A cover of Z covers each point J in Z and therefore its U_J term, so T preserves covering sieves.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi, proof; finite-nonempty-subset variant of the auxiliary space

proof.text: The intersection identity verifies CompatiblePreserving directly: restrict the compatibility equation on Z intersection W to the given common subopen of T(Z) and T(W). Together with cover preservation, Mathlib Functor.isContinuous_of_coverPreserving proves continuity on the open sites. Functor.op_comp_isSheaf constructs G0=T.op composed with F. Compose with AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor to put coefficients in the same universe as P; this functor preserves limits and hence the sheaf property.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi, proof; finite-nonempty-subset variant of the auxiliary space

proof.text: The hypothesis hres applied to S={J | J belongs to Z} makes F(U) to F(T(Z)) surjective. For Z contained in W, extend any section to U and restrict to T(W); functoriality makes its restriction to T(Z) the given section. Lifting sections by ULift preserves this argument and proves G flasque.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi, proof; finite-nonempty-subset variant of the auxiliary space

proof.text: For a tuple t, T(intersection_k B_{singleton t(k)})=intersection_k U_{t(k)}. The universal property of the supplied SiteCechComplex identifies K.W p t with this open. Componentwise restriction along this equality and ULift give additive isomorphisms of cochains. The two alternating differentials commute with them: distribute restriction and ULift.down over the signed finite sum, and use thinness of the open category to identify each pair of composite restriction arrows. Hom.isoOfComponents assembles the resulting complex isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A36, lemma-vanishing-ravi, proof; finite-nonempty-subset variant of the auxiliary space

proof.text: Apply TopCat.Sheaf.exactAt_cechComplex_of_isFlasque to G and the singleton basic-open family. Its exactness in degree q+1 transports across the inverse complex isomorphism to K.complex F. ExactAt.isZero_homology proves the conclusion for every p>0 by writing p=q+1.
